title: Evaluate network protocols, routing, and infrastructure design: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: For this flow, who receives it, which path/plane carries it, where does protection terminate, and what shared dependency can fail?
focalInsight: Addressing, delivery type, topology, plane separation, and cryptographic endpoints jointly determine actual reachability and failure exposure.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Osi Model
nodes.definition: Layered vocabulary for locating protocol functions and associated security threats.
nodes.detail: Layered vocabulary for locating protocol functions and associated security threats.
nodes.decision: Identify the functional layer before selecting inspection, routing, session, or application controls.
nodes.failureExample: Applying only a network filter to an application-layer abuse case leaves the vulnerable function exposed.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Use OSI to locate the function, not to assume a control is sufficient.

nodes.label: Tcp Ip Model
nodes.definition: Internet protocol-suite model used to reason about deployed addressing, transport, and application communication.
nodes.detail: Internet protocol-suite model used to reason about deployed addressing, transport, and application communication.
nodes.decision: Use it with actual packet/session endpoints and map to OSI when comparing functions.
nodes.failureExample: Treating transport reliability as application authorization confuses stack responsibilities.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: TCP/IP explains deployed protocol roles; it does not grant trust.

nodes.label: Ipv4
nodes.definition: IP address family with unicast, local broadcast, and multicast reachability behavior.
nodes.detail: IP address family with unicast, local broadcast, and multicast reachability behavior.
nodes.decision: Identify scope and broadcast implications before routing/filtering a flow.
nodes.failureExample: Broadcast permission on a sensitive segment expands recipient exposure.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: IPv4 broadcast targets a local domain, not a chosen host.

nodes.label: Ipv6
nodes.definition: IP address family using unicast, multicast, and anycast rather than IPv4 broadcast.
nodes.detail: IP address family using unicast, multicast, and anycast rather than IPv4 broadcast.
nodes.decision: Implement explicit IPv6 routing, discovery, ACL, and telemetry policy in dual-stack environments.
nodes.failureExample: Ignoring IPv6 lets a host bypass IPv4-only inspection.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: IPv6 has no IPv4-style broadcast; account for multicast/anycast.

nodes.label: Ipv4 Ipv6
nodes.definition: Coexistence/transition state in which both address families may expose parallel routes and policies.
nodes.detail: Coexistence/transition state in which both address families may expose parallel routes and policies.
nodes.decision: Test every service, management path, ACL, monitor, and tunnel for both families.
nodes.failureExample: A secure IPv4 design is bypassed through an unlogged IPv6 listener.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Treat each family as a separately verified path.

nodes.label: unicast
nodes.definition: Delivery from one sender to one addressed receiver.
nodes.detail: Delivery from one sender to one addressed receiver.
nodes.decision: Use when a single intended endpoint and its authorization/path are known.
nodes.failureExample: Assuming unicast means trusted destination ignores endpoint compromise.

nodes.label: Multicast
nodes.definition: Delivery to members of an explicitly managed group.
nodes.detail: Delivery to members of an explicitly managed group.
nodes.decision: Control membership, scope, routing, and monitoring before enabling.
nodes.failureExample: Uncontrolled membership receives sensitive telemetry intended for a service group.

nodes.label: Traffic Monitoring
nodes.definition: Collection and analysis of traffic/flow evidence for behavior, capacity, policy, and anomaly detection.
nodes.detail: Collection and analysis of traffic/flow evidence for behavior, capacity, policy, and anomaly detection.
nodes.decision: Place sensors where visibility survives encapsulation/termination and protect their management/data paths.
nodes.failureExample: A monitor before TLS termination cannot inspect protected application content.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Monitoring point must match the evidence question.

nodes.label: Ipsec
nodes.definition: Network-layer protection between defined IPsec peers and traffic selectors.
nodes.detail: Network-layer protection between defined IPsec peers and traffic selectors.
nodes.decision: Verify peer authentication, selectors, key renewal, path/intermediary handling, logs, and onward protection.
nodes.failureExample: Encrypting to a gateway does not authorize access beyond it.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: IPsec endpoint and selector define protected traffic.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: For this flow, who receives it, which path/plane carries it, where does protection terminate, and what shared dependency can fail?
learningContract.misconception: An IP address, tunnel, or redundant link alone tells you the audience, trust boundary, or resilience outcome.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned rows make each network term answer a distinct design, security, and failure question.
learningContract.focalInsight: Addressing, delivery type, topology, plane separation, and cryptographic endpoints jointly determine actual reachability and failure exposure.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Implementation settings and jurisdiction-specific conclusions are not inferred from these concise concept comparisons.
